verses.english: Long Discourses 21
Sakka’s Questions
So I have heard.

verses.pali: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā magadhesu viharati, pācīnato rājagahassa ambasaṇḍā nāma brāhmaṇagāmo, tassuttarato vediyake pabbate indasālaguhāyaṁ.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Magadhans, where east of Rājagaha there is a brahmin village named Ambasaṇḍā, north of which, on Mount Vediyaka, is Indra’s hill cave.

verses.pali: Tena kho pana samayena sakkassa devānamindassa ussukkaṁ udapādi bhagavantaṁ dassanāya.
verses.english: Now at that time Sakka, the lord of gods, grew eager to see the Buddha.
He thought,

verses.pali: “kahaṁ nu kho bhagavā etarahi viharati arahaṁ sammāsambuddho”ti?
verses.english: “Where is the Blessed One at present, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha?”

verses.pali: Addasā kho sakko devānamindo bhagavantaṁ magadhesu viharantaṁ pācīnato rājagahassa ambasaṇḍā nāma brāhmaṇagāmo, tassuttarato vediyake pabbate indasālaguhāyaṁ.
verses.english: Seeing that the Buddha was at Indra’s hill cave,
he addressed the gods of the thirty-three,

verses.pali: “ayaṁ, mārisā, bhagavā magadhesu viharati, pācīnato rājagahassa ambasaṇḍā nāma brāhmaṇagāmo, tassuttarato vediyake pabbate indasālaguhāyaṁ.
verses.english: “Good fellows, the Buddha is staying in the land of the Magadhans at Indra’s hill cave.

verses.pali: Yadi pana, mārisā, mayaṁ taṁ bhagavantaṁ dassanāya upasaṅkameyyāma arahantaṁ sammāsambuddhan”ti?
verses.english: What if we were to go and see that Blessed One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha?”

verses.pali: “Evaṁ, bhaddantavā”ti kho devā tāvatiṁsā sakkassa devānamindassa paccassosuṁ.
verses.english: “Yes, lord,” replied the gods.

verses.pali: Atha kho sakko devānamindo pañcasikhaṁ gandhabbadevaputtaṁ āmantesi:
verses.english: Then Sakka addressed the centaur Pañcasikha,

verses.pali: “ayaṁ, tāta pañcasikha, bhagavā magadhesu viharati pācīnato rājagahassa ambasaṇḍā nāma brāhmaṇagāmo, tassuttarato vediyake pabbate indasālaguhāyaṁ.
verses.english: “Dear Pañcasikha, the Buddha is staying in the land of the Magadhans at Indra’s hill cave.

verses.pali: Yadi pana, tāta pañcasikha, mayaṁ taṁ bhagavantaṁ dassanāya upasaṅkameyyāma arahantaṁ sammāsambuddhan”ti?
verses.english: What if we were to go and see that Blessed One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha?”

verses.pali: “Evaṁ, bhaddantavā”ti kho pañcasikho gandhabbadevaputto sakkassa devānamindassa paṭissutvā beluvapaṇḍuvīṇaṁ ādāya sakkassa devānamindassa anucariyaṁ upāgami.
verses.english: “Yes, lord,” replied the centaur Pañcasikha. Taking his arched harp made from the pale timber of wood-apple, he went as Sakka’s attendant.

verses.pali: Atha kho sakko devānamindo devehi tāvatiṁsehi parivuto pañcasikhena gandhabbadevaputtena purakkhato—
verses.english: Then Sakka went at the head of a retinue consisting of the gods of the thirty-three and the godling centaur Pañcasikha.

verses.pali: seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṁ vā bāhaṁ pasāreyya pasāritaṁ vā bāhaṁ samiñjeyya; evameva—devesu tāvatiṁsesu antarahito magadhesu pācīnato rājagahassa ambasaṇḍā nāma brāhmaṇagāmo, tassuttarato vediyake pabbate paccuṭṭhāsi.
verses.english: As easily as a strong person would extend or contract their arm, he vanished from the heaven of the gods of the thirty-three and landed on Mount Vediyaka north of Ambasaṇḍā.

verses.pali: Tena kho pana samayena vediyako pabbato atiriva obhāsajāto hoti ambasaṇḍā ca brāhmaṇagāmo yathā taṁ devānaṁ devānubhāvena.
verses.english: Now at that time a dazzling light appeared over Mount Vediyaka and Ambasaṇḍā, as happens through the glory of the gods.
People in the villages round about, terrified, shocked, and awestruck, said,

verses.pali: “ādittassu nāmajja vediyako pabbato jhāyatisu nāmajja vediyako pabbato jalatisu. Nāmajja vediyako pabbato.
verses.english: “Mount Vediyaka must be on fire today, blazing and burning!

verses.pali: Kiṁsu nāmajja vediyako pabbato atiriva obhāsajāto ambasaṇḍā ca brāhmaṇagāmo”ti;
verses.english: Oh why has such a dazzling light appeared over Mount Vediyaka and Ambasaṇḍā?”

verses.pali: Atha kho sakko devānamindo pañcasikhaṁ gandhabbadevaputtaṁ āmantesi:
verses.english: Then Sakka addressed the centaur Pañcasikha,

verses.pali: “durupasaṅkamā kho, tāta pañcasikha, tathāgatā mādisena, jhāyī jhānaratā, tadantaraṁ paṭisallīnā.
verses.english: “My dear Pañcasikha, it is hard for one like me to get near the Realized Ones while they are on retreat practicing absorption, enjoying absorption.

verses.pali: Yadi pana tvaṁ, tāta pañcasikha, bhagavantaṁ paṭhamaṁ pasādeyyāsi, tayā, tāta, paṭhamaṁ pasāditaṁ pacchā mayaṁ taṁ bhagavantaṁ dassanāya upasaṅkameyyāma arahantaṁ sammāsambuddhan”ti.
verses.english: But if you were to charm the Buddha first, then I could go to see him.”

verses.pali: “Evaṁ, bhaddantavā”ti kho pañcasikho gandhabbadevaputto sakkassa devānamindassa paṭissutvā beluvapaṇḍuvīṇaṁ ādāya yena indasālaguhā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā:
verses.english: “Yes, lord,” replied the centaur Pañcasikha. Taking his arched harp made from the pale timber of wood-apple, he went to Indra’s hill cave. When he had drawn near, he stood to one side, thinking,

verses.pali: “ettāvatā me bhagavā neva atidūre bhavissati nāccāsanne, saddañca me sossatī”ti—
verses.english: “This is neither too far nor too near; and he’ll hear my voice.”
1. Pañcasikha’s Song

verses.pali: Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho pañcasikho gandhabbadevaputto beluvapaṇḍuvīṇaṁ assāvesi, imā ca gāthā abhāsi buddhūpasañhitā dhammūpasañhitā saṅghūpasañhitā arahantūpasañhitā kāmūpasañhitā:
verses.english: Standing to one side, Pañcasikha played his arched harp, and sang these verses on the Buddha, the teaching, the Saṅgha, the perfected ones, and sensual love.
“O Bhaddā Suriyavaccasā, my Darling Sunshine,
I pay homage to your father Timbaru,
through whom was born a lady so fine,
to fill me with a joy I never knew.
As sweet as a breeze to one who’s sweating,
or when thirsty, a sweet and cooling drink,
so dear are you, Aṅgīrasi, to me—
just like the teaching is to all the saints!
Like a cure when you’re struck by fever dire,
or food to ease the hunger pain,
come on, Bhaddā, please put out my fire,
quench me like water on a flame.
As elephants burning in the heat of summer,
sink down in a lotus pond to rest,
so cool, full of petals and of pollen—
that’s how I would plunge into your breast.
Like elephants bursting bonds in rutting season,
beating off the pricks of lance and pikes—
I just don’t understand what is the reason
I’m so crazy for your shapely thighs!
For you, my heart is full of passion,
I’m in a besotted state of mind.
There is no going back, I’m just not able,
I’m like a fish that’s hooked up on the line.
Come on, my Bhaddā, hold me, fair of thighs!
Embrace me, maid of captivating eyes!
Take me in your arms, my lovely lady,
that’s all I’d ever want or could desire.
Ah, then my desire was such a small thing,
my sweet, with your curling wavy hair;
now, like to arahants an offering,
it’s grown so very much from there.
Whatever the merit I have forged
by giving to such perfected beings—
may that, my altogether gorgeous,
ripen in togetherness with you.
Whatever the merit I have forged
in this vast territory,
may that, my altogether gorgeous,
ripen in togetherness with you.
As the Sakyan, absorbed, did meditate
at one, alert, and mindful too,
the sage seeking the state free of death—
so I, oh my Sunshine, seek for you!
And just like the sage would delight,
once he had awakened to the truth,
so I would delight, my fine lady,
were I to become one with you.
If Sakka were to grant me one wish,
as Lord of the Thirty and Three,
my Bhaddā, you’re all I would wish for,
so strong is the love in me.
Like a freshly blossoming sal tree
is your father, my lady so wise.
I pay homage to he, bowing humbly,
whose daughter is of such a kind.”

verses.pali: Evaṁ vutte, bhagavā pañcasikhaṁ gandhabbadevaputtaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: When Pañcasikha had spoken, the Buddha said to him,

verses.pali: “saṁsandati kho te, pañcasikha, tantissaro gītassarena, gītassaro ca tantissarena;
verses.english: “Pañcasikha, the sound of your strings blends well with the sound of your singing,

verses.pali: na ca pana te, pañcasikha, tantissaro gītassaraṁ ativattati, gītassaro ca tantissaraṁ.
verses.english: so that neither overpowers the other.

verses.pali: Kadā saṁyūḷhā pana te, pañcasikha, imā gāthā buddhūpasañhitā dhammūpasañhitā saṅghūpasañhitā arahantūpasañhitā kāmūpasañhitā”ti?
verses.english: But when did you compose these verses on the Buddha, the teaching, the Saṅgha, the perfected ones, and sensual love?”

verses.pali: “Ekamidaṁ, bhante, samayaṁ bhagavā uruvelāyaṁ viharati najjā nerañjarāya tīre ajapālanigrodhe paṭhamābhisambuddho.
verses.english: “This one time, sir, when you were first awakened, you were staying in Uruvelā at the goatherd’s banyan tree on the bank of the Nerañjarā River.

verses.pali: Tena kho panāhaṁ, bhante, samayena bhaddā nāma sūriyavacchasā timbaruno gandhabbarañño dhītā, tamabhikaṅkhāmi.
verses.english: And at that time I was in love with Bhaddā Suriyavaccasā, who they call ‘Darling Sunshine’, the daughter of the centaur king Timbaru.

verses.pali: Sā kho pana, bhante, bhaginī parakāminī hoti;
verses.english: But the sister desired another.

verses.pali: sikhaṇḍī nāma mātalissa saṅgāhakassa putto, tamabhikaṅkhati.
verses.english: It was the one named Sikhaṇḍī, the son of Mātali the chariot handler, who she loved.

verses.pali: Yato kho ahaṁ, bhante, taṁ bhaginiṁ nālatthaṁ kenaci pariyāyena.
verses.english: Since I couldn’t win that sister by any means,

verses.pali: Athāhaṁ beluvapaṇḍuvīṇaṁ ādāya yena timbaruno gandhabbarañño nivesanaṁ tenupasaṅkamiṁ; upasaṅkamitvā beluvapaṇḍuvīṇaṁ assāvesiṁ, imā ca gāthā abhāsiṁ buddhūpasañhitā dhammūpasañhitā saṅghūpasañhitā arahantūpasañhitā kāmūpasañhitā—
verses.english: I took my arched harp to Timbaru’s home, where I played those verses.

verses.pali: Evaṁ vutte, bhante, bhaddā sūriyavacchasā maṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: When I finished, Suriyavaccasā said to me,

verses.pali: ‘na kho me, mārisa, so bhagavā sammukhā diṭṭho, api ca sutoyeva me so bhagavā devānaṁ tāvatiṁsānaṁ sudhammāyaṁ sabhāyaṁ upanaccantiyā.
verses.english: ‘Good fellow, I have not personally seen the Buddha. But I did hear about him when I went to dance for the gods of the thirty-three in the Hall of Clear Right.

verses.pali: Yato kho tvaṁ, mārisa, taṁ bhagavantaṁ kittesi, hotu no ajja samāgamo’ti.
verses.english: Since you extol the Buddha, let us meet up today.’

verses.pali: Soyeva no, bhante, tassā bhaginiyā saddhiṁ samāgamo ahosi.
verses.english: And that’s when I met up with that sister.
But we have not met since.”
2. The Approach of Sakka
Then Sakka, lord of gods, thought,

verses.pali: “paṭisammodati pañcasikho gandhabbadevaputto bhagavatā, bhagavā ca pañcasikhenā”ti.
verses.english: “Pañcasikha is exchanging pleasantries with the Buddha.”

verses.pali: Atha kho sakko devānamindo pañcasikhaṁ gandhabbadevaputtaṁ āmantesi:
verses.english: So he addressed Pañcasikha,
“My dear Pañcasikha, please bow to the Buddha for me, saying:

verses.pali: ‘sakko, bhante, devānamindo sāmacco saparijano bhagavato pāde sirasā vandatī’”ti.
verses.english: ‘Sir, Sakka, lord of gods, with his ministers and retinue, bows with his head at your feet.’”

verses.pali: “Evaṁ, bhaddantavā”ti kho pañcasikho gandhabbadevaputto sakkassa devānamindassa paṭissutvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādeti:
verses.english: “Yes, lord,” replied Pañcasikha. He bowed to the Buddha and said,

verses.pali: “sakko, bhante, devānamindo sāmacco saparijano bhagavato pāde sirasā vandatī”ti.
verses.english: “Sir, Sakka, lord of gods, with his ministers and retinue, bows with his head at your feet.”

verses.pali: “Evaṁ sukhī hotu, pañcasikha, sakko devānamindo sāmacco saparijano;
verses.english: “So may Sakka with his ministers and retinue be happy, Pañcasikha,” said the Buddha,

verses.pali: sukhakāmā hi devā manussā asurā nāgā gandhabbā ye caññe santi puthukāyā”ti.
verses.english: “for all want to be happy—whether gods, humans, titans, dragons, centaurs, or any of the other diverse creatures there may be.”

verses.pali: Evañca pana tathāgatā evarūpe mahesakkhe yakkhe abhivadanti.
verses.english: For that is how the Realized Ones salute such illustrious spirits.

verses.pali: Abhivadito sakko devānamindo bhagavato indasālaguhaṁ pavisitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi.
verses.english: And being saluted by the Buddha, Sakka entered Indra’s hill cave, bowed to the Buddha, and stood to one side.

verses.pali: Devāpi tāvatiṁsā indasālaguhaṁ pavisitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhaṁsu.
verses.english: And the gods of the thirty-three did likewise,

verses.pali: Pañcasikhopi gandhabbadevaputto indasālaguhaṁ pavisitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi.
verses.english: as did Pañcasikha.

verses.pali: Tena kho pana samayena indasālaguhā visamā santī samā samapādi, sambādhā santī urundā samapādi, andhakāro guhāyaṁ antaradhāyi, āloko udapādi yathā taṁ devānaṁ devānubhāvena.
verses.english: And at that time the uneven places were evened out, the cramped places were opened up, the darkness vanished in the cave and light appeared, as happens through the glory of the gods.

verses.pali: Atha kho bhagavā sakkaṁ devānamindaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: Then the Buddha said to Sakka,

verses.pali: “acchariyamidaṁ āyasmato kosiyassa, abbhutamidaṁ āyasmato kosiyassa tāva bahukiccassa bahukaraṇīyassa yadidaṁ idhāgamanan”ti.
verses.english: “It’s incredible and amazing that you, the venerable Kosiya, who has so many duties and so much to do, should come here.”

verses.pali: “Cirapaṭikāhaṁ, bhante, bhagavantaṁ dassanāya upasaṅkamitukāmo; api ca devānaṁ tāvatiṁsānaṁ kehici kehici kiccakaraṇīyehi byāvaṭo; evāhaṁ nāsakkhiṁ bhagavantaṁ dassanāya upasaṅkamituṁ.
verses.english: “For a long time I’ve wanted to come and see the Buddha, but I wasn’t able, being prevented by my many duties and responsibilities for the gods of the thirty-three.

verses.pali: Ekamidaṁ, bhante, samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati salaḷāgārake.
verses.english: This one time, sir, the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in the salaḷa tree hut.

verses.pali: Atha khvāhaṁ, bhante, sāvatthiṁ agamāsiṁ bhagavantaṁ dassanāya.
verses.english: Then I went to Sāvatthī to see the Buddha.

verses.pali: Tena kho pana, bhante, samayena bhagavā aññatarena samādhinā nisinno hoti, bhūjati ca nāma vessavaṇassa mahārājassa paricārikā bhagavantaṁ paccupaṭṭhitā hoti, pañjalikā namassamānā tiṭṭhati.
verses.english: But at that time the Buddha was sitting immersed in some kind of meditation. And a divine maiden of Great King Vessavaṇa named Bhūjati was attending on the Buddha, standing there paying homage to him with cupped palms.
So I said to her,
‘Sister, please bow to the Buddha for me, saying:

verses.pali: “sakko, bhante, devānamindo sāmacco saparijano bhagavato pāde sirasā vandatī”’ti.
verses.english: “Sir, Sakka, lord of gods, with his ministers and retinue, bows with his head at your feet.”’

verses.pali: Evaṁ vutte, bhante, sā bhūjati maṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: When I said this, she said to me,
‘It’s the wrong time to see the Buddha,
as he’s in retreat.’

verses.pali: ‘Tena hi, bhagini, yadā bhagavā tamhā samādhimhā vuṭṭhito hoti, atha mama vacanena bhagavantaṁ abhivādehi:
verses.english: ‘Well then, sister, please convey my message when the Buddha emerges from that immersion.’

verses.pali: “sakko, bhante, devānamindo sāmacco saparijano bhagavato pāde sirasā vandatī”’ti.
Kacci me sā, bhante, bhaginī bhagavantaṁ abhivādesi?
verses.english: I hope that sister bowed to you?
Do you remember what she said?”

verses.pali: “Abhivādesi maṁ sā, devānaminda, bhaginī, sarāmahaṁ tassā bhaginiyā vacanaṁ.
verses.english: “She did bow, lord of gods, and I remember what she said.

verses.pali: Api cāhaṁ āyasmato nemisaddena tamhā samādhimhā vuṭṭhito”ti.
verses.english: I also remember that it was the sound of your chariot wheels that pulled me out of that immersion.”

verses.pali: “Ye te, bhante, devā amhehi paṭhamataraṁ tāvatiṁsakāyaṁ upapannā, tesaṁ me sammukhā sutaṁ sammukhā paṭiggahitaṁ:
verses.english: “Sir, I have heard and learned this in the presence of the gods who were reborn in the host of the thirty-three before me:

verses.pali: ‘yadā tathāgatā loke uppajjanti arahanto sammāsambuddhā, dibbā kāyā paripūrenti, hāyanti asurakāyā’ti.
verses.english: ‘When a Realized One arises in the world, perfected and fully awakened, the heavenly hosts swell, while the titan hosts dwindle.’

verses.pali: Taṁ me idaṁ, bhante, sakkhidiṭṭhaṁ yato tathāgato loke uppanno arahaṁ sammāsambuddho, dibbā kāyā paripūrenti, hāyanti asurakāyāti.
verses.english: And I have seen this with my own eyes.
2.1. The Story of Gopikā

verses.pali: Idheva, bhante, kapilavatthusmiṁ gopikā nāma sakyadhītā ahosi buddhe pasannā dhamme pasannā saṅghe pasannā sīlesu paripūrakārinī.
verses.english: Right here in Kapilavatthu there was a Sakyan lady named Gopikā who had confidence in the Buddha, the teaching, and the Saṅgha, and had fulfilled her ethics.

verses.pali: Sā itthittaṁ virājetvā purisattaṁ bhāvetvā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapannā.
verses.english: Losing her attachment to femininity, she developed masculinity. When her body broke up, after death, she was reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

verses.pali: Devānaṁ tāvatiṁsānaṁ sahabyataṁ amhākaṁ puttattaṁ ajjhupagatā.
verses.english: In the company of the gods of the thirty-three she became one of my sons.
There they knew him as
the godling Gopaka.

verses.pali: Aññepi, bhante, tayo bhikkhū bhagavati brahmacariyaṁ caritvā hīnaṁ gandhabbakāyaṁ upapannā.
verses.english: Meanwhile three others, mendicants who had led the spiritual life under the Buddha, were reborn in the inferior centaur realm.

verses.pali: Te pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappitā samaṅgībhūtā paricārayamānā amhākaṁ upaṭṭhānaṁ āgacchanti amhākaṁ pāricariyaṁ.
verses.english: There they amused themselves, supplied and provided with the five kinds of sensual stimulation, and became my servants and attendants.

verses.pali: Te amhākaṁ upaṭṭhānaṁ āgate amhākaṁ pāricariyaṁ gopako devaputto paṭicodesi:
verses.english: At that, Gopaka scolded them,

verses.pali: ‘kutomukhā nāma tumhe, mārisā, tassa bhagavato dhammaṁ assuttha—
verses.english: ‘Where on earth were you at, good fellows, when you heard the Buddha’s teaching!

verses.pali: ahañhi nāma itthikā samānā buddhe pasannā dhamme pasannā saṅghe pasannā sīlesu paripūrakārinī itthittaṁ virājetvā purisattaṁ bhāvetvā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapannā, devānaṁ tāvatiṁsānaṁ sahabyataṁ sakkassa devānamindassa puttattaṁ ajjhupagatā.
verses.english: For while I was still a woman I had confidence in the Buddha, the teaching, and the Saṅgha, and had fulfilled my ethics. I lost my attachment to femininity and developed masculinity. When my body broke up, after death, I was reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm. In the company of the gods of the thirty-three I became one of Sakka’s sons.
Here they know me as
the godling Gopaka.

verses.pali: Tumhe pana, mārisā, bhagavati brahmacariyaṁ caritvā hīnaṁ gandhabbakāyaṁ upapannā.
verses.english: But you, having led the spiritual life under the Buddha, were reborn in the inferior centaur realm.

verses.pali: Duddiṭṭharūpaṁ vata bho addasāma, ye mayaṁ addasāma sahadhammike hīnaṁ gandhabbakāyaṁ upapanne’ti.
verses.english: It is a sad sight indeed to see fellow practitioners reborn in the inferior centaur realm.’

verses.pali: Tesaṁ, bhante, gopakena devaputtena paṭicoditānaṁ dve devā diṭṭheva dhamme satiṁ paṭilabhiṁsu kāyaṁ brahmapurohitaṁ, eko pana devo kāme ajjhāvasi.
verses.english: When scolded by Gopaka, two of those gods regained their memory right away. They went to the host of the priests of Divinity, but one god remained attached to sensual pleasures.
‘“I was a laywoman disciple of the Clear-eyed One,
and my name was Gopikā.
I was devoted to the Buddha and the teaching,
and I faithfully served the Saṅgha.
Because of the clear rightness of the Buddha’s teaching,
I’m now a mighty, dazzling son of Sakka,
reborn in the Third Heaven.
And here they know me as Gopaka.
Then I saw some mendicants who I’d seen before,
dwelling in the host of centaurs.
They were disciples of Gotama
when I used to be a human.
I served them with food and drink,
and clasped their feet in my own home.
Where on earth were these good fellows at
when they learned the Buddha’s teachings?
For each must know for themselves the teaching
so well-taught, realized by the Clear-eyed One.
I was one who followed you,
having heard the fine words of the noble ones.
I’m now a mighty, dazzling son of Sakka,
reborn in the Third Heaven.
But you followed the best of men,
and led the supreme spiritual life,
but still you’re born in this lesser realm,
a rebirth unbefitting.
It’s a sad sight I see, good fellows,
fellow practitioners in a lesser realm.
Reborn in the host of centaurs,
only to wait upon the gods.
Meanwhile, I dwelt in a house—
but see my distinction now!
Having been a woman now I’m a male god,
blessed with heavenly sensual pleasures.”
Scolded by that disciple of Gotama,
comprehending Gopaka, <j>they were struck with urgency.
“Let’s strive, let’s try hard—
we won’t serve others any more!”
Two of them roused up energy,
recalling the Buddha’s instructions.
Right away they became dispassionate,
seeing the drawbacks in sensual pleasures.
The fetters and bonds of sensual pleasures—
the ties of the Wicked One so hard to break—
they burst them like a bull elephant his ropes,
and passed right over the thirty-three.
The gods with Indra and the Progenitor
were all gathered in the Hall of Clear Right.
As they sat there, they passed over them,
the heroes desireless, practicing purity.
Seeing them, Vāsava was struck with urgency;
the master of gods in the midst of the group said,
“These were born in the lesser centaur realm,
but now they pass us by!”
Heeding the speech of one so moved,
Gopaka addressed Vāsava,
“There is a Buddha, a lord of men, in the world.
Known as the Sakyan Sage, <j>he’s mastered the senses.
Those sons of his lost their memory;
but when scolded by me they gained it back.
Of the three, there is one who remains
dwelling in the host of centaurs.
But two, recollecting the path to awakening,
serene, spurn even the gods.
Such is the explanation of the teaching here:
not a single disciple doubts that.
We venerate the Buddha, the victor, lord of men,
who has crossed the flood and cut off doubt.
They attained distinction to the extent
they understood the teaching here;
two of them distinguished
in the host of the priests of Divinity.”’
We have come here, dear sir,
to realize this same teaching.
If the Buddha would give me a chance,
I would ask a question, dear sir.”
Then it occurred to the Buddha,

verses.pali: “dīgharattaṁ visuddho kho ayaṁ yakkho, yaṁ kiñci maṁ pañhaṁ pucchissati, sabbaṁ taṁ atthasañhitaṁyeva pucchissati, no anatthasañhitaṁ.
verses.english: “For a long time now this spirit has led a pure life. Any question he asks me will be beneficial, not unbeneficial.

verses.pali: Yañcassāhaṁ puṭṭho byākarissāmi, taṁ khippameva ājānissatī”ti.
verses.english: And he will quickly understand any answer I give to his question.”

verses.pali: Atha kho bhagavā sakkaṁ devānamindaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
verses.english: So the Buddha addressed Sakka in verse:
“Ask me your question, Vāsava,
whatever you want.
I’ll solve each and every
question you have.”
The first recitation section is finished.

verses.pali: Katāvakāso sakko devānamindo bhagavatā imaṁ bhagavantaṁ paṭhamaṁ pañhaṁ apucchi:

There are two kinds of search, I say:

There are two kinds of sound known by the ear …
smells known by the nose …
tastes known by the tongue …
touches known by the body …
ideas known by the mind:
that which you should cultivate, and that which you should not cultivate.”

verses.pali: Tasmiṁ anekadhātunānādhātusmiṁ loke yaṁ yadeva sattā dhātuṁ abhinivisanti, taṁ tadeva thāmasā parāmāsā abhinivissa voharanti:
verses.english: Whatever element sentient beings insist on in this world of many and diverse elements, they obstinately stick to it, insisting that:
‘This is the only truth, anything else is futile.’

verses.pali: Tasmā na sabbe samaṇabrāhmaṇā ekantavādā ekantasīlā ekantachandā ekantaajjhosānā”ti.
verses.english: That’s why not all ascetics and brahmins have a single doctrine, ethics, desire, and attachment.”

verses.pali: “Sabbeva nu kho, mārisa, samaṇabrāhmaṇā accantaniṭṭhā accantayogakkhemī accantabrahmacārī accantapariyosānā”ti?
verses.english: “Good fellow, have all ascetics and brahmins reached the ultimate end, the ultimate sanctuary from the yoke, the ultimate spiritual life, the ultimate goal?”

verses.pali: “Na kho, devānaminda, sabbe samaṇabrāhmaṇā accantaniṭṭhā accantayogakkhemī accantabrahmacārī accantapariyosānā”ti.
verses.english: “No, lord of gods, they have not.”

verses.pali: “Kasmā pana, mārisa, na sabbe samaṇabrāhmaṇā accantaniṭṭhā accantayogakkhemī accantabrahmacārī accantapariyosānā”ti?
verses.english: “Why not?”

verses.pali: “Ye kho, devānaminda, bhikkhū taṇhāsaṅkhayavimuttā te accantaniṭṭhā accantayogakkhemī accantabrahmacārī accantapariyosānā.
verses.english: “Those mendicants who are freed through the ending of craving have reached the ultimate end, the ultimate sanctuary from the yoke, the ultimate spiritual life, the ultimate goal.

verses.pali: Tasmā na sabbe samaṇabrāhmaṇā accantaniṭṭhā accantayogakkhemī accantabrahmacārī accantapariyosānā”ti.
verses.english: That’s why not all ascetics and brahmins have reached the ultimate end, the ultimate sanctuary from the yoke, the ultimate spiritual life, the ultimate goal.”

verses.pali: Itthaṁ bhagavā sakkassa devānamindassa pañhaṁ puṭṭho byākāsi.
verses.english: Such was the Buddha’s answer to Sakka.

verses.pali: Attamano sakko devānamindo bhagavato bhāsitaṁ abhinandi anumodi:
verses.english: Delighted, Sakka approved and agreed with what the Buddha said, saying,
“That’s so true, Blessed One! That’s so true, Holy One!

verses.pali: Tiṇṇā mettha kaṅkhā vigatā kathaṅkathā bhagavato pañhaveyyākaraṇaṁ sutvā”ti.
verses.english: Hearing the Buddha’s answer, I’ve gone beyond doubt and got rid of indecision.”

verses.pali: Itiha sakko devānamindo bhagavato bhāsitaṁ abhinanditvā anumoditvā bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: And then Sakka, having approved and agreed with what the Buddha said, said to him,

verses.pali: “Ejā, bhante, rogo, ejā gaṇḍo, ejā sallaṁ, ejā imaṁ purisaṁ parikaḍḍhati tassa tasseva bhavassa abhinibbattiyā.
verses.english: “Turbulence, sir, is a disease, a boil, a dart. Turbulence drags a person to be regenerated in one state of existence or another.
That’s why a person finds themselves in states high and low.

verses.pali: Yesāhaṁ, bhante, pañhānaṁ ito bahiddhā aññesu samaṇabrāhmaṇesu okāsakammampi nālatthaṁ, te me bhagavatā byākatā.
verses.english: Elsewhere, among other ascetics and brahmins, I wasn’t even given a chance to ask these questions that the Buddha has answered.

verses.pali: Dīgharattānusayitañca pana me vicikicchākathaṅkathāsallaṁ, tañca bhagavatā abbuḷhan”ti.
verses.english: The dart of doubt and indecision has lain within me for a long time, but the Buddha has plucked it out.”

verses.pali: “Abhijānāsi no tvaṁ, devānaminda, ime pañhe aññe samaṇabrāhmaṇe pucchitā”ti?
verses.english: “Lord of gods, do you recall having asked this question of other ascetics and brahmins?”

verses.pali: “Abhijānāmahaṁ, bhante, ime pañhe aññe samaṇabrāhmaṇe pucchitā”ti.
verses.english: “I do, sir.”

verses.pali: “Yathā kathaṁ pana te, devānaminda, byākaṁsu? Sace te agaru bhāsassū”ti.
verses.english: “If you wouldn’t mind, lord of gods, tell me how they answered.”

verses.pali: “Na kho me, bhante, garu yatthassa bhagavā nisinno bhagavantarūpo vā”ti.
verses.english: “It’s no trouble when someone such as the Blessed One is sitting here.”
“Well, speak then, lord of gods.”

verses.pali: “Yesvāhaṁ, bhante, maññāmi samaṇabrāhmaṇā āraññikā pantasenāsanāti, tyāhaṁ upasaṅkamitvā ime pañhe pucchāmi, te mayā puṭṭhā na sampāyanti, asampāyantā mamaṁyeva paṭipucchanti:
verses.english: “Sir, I approached those who I imagined were ascetics and brahmins living in the wilderness, in remote lodgings. But they were stumped by my question, and they even questioned me in return:
‘What is the venerable’s name?’
So I answered them:
‘Good fellow, I am Sakka, lord of gods.’
So they asked me another question:

verses.pali: ‘kiṁ panāyasmā, devānaminda, kammaṁ katvā imaṁ ṭhānaṁ patto’ti?
verses.english: ‘But lord of gods, what deed brought you to this position?’
So I taught them the Dhamma as I had learned and memorized it.
And they were pleased with just that much:

verses.pali: ‘sakko ca no devānamindo diṭṭho, yañca no apucchimhā, tañca no byākāsī’ti.
verses.english: ‘We have seen Sakka, lord of gods! And he answered our questions!’

verses.pali: Te aññadatthu mamaṁyeva sāvakā sampajjanti, na cāhaṁ tesaṁ.
verses.english: Invariably, they become my disciples, I don’t become theirs.

verses.pali: Ahaṁ kho pana, bhante, bhagavato sāvako sotāpanno avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo”ti.
verses.english: But sir, I am the Buddha’s disciple, a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.”
2.5. On Feeling Happy

verses.pali: “Abhijānāsi no tvaṁ, devānaminda, ito pubbe evarūpaṁ vedapaṭilābhaṁ somanassapaṭilābhan”ti?
verses.english: “Lord of gods, do you recall ever feeling such joy and happiness before?”

verses.pali: “Abhijānāmahaṁ, bhante, ito pubbe evarūpaṁ vedapaṭilābhaṁ somanassapaṭilābhan”ti.
verses.english: “I do, sir.”

verses.pali: “Yathā kathaṁ pana tvaṁ, devānaminda, abhijānāsi ito pubbe evarūpaṁ vedapaṭilābhaṁ somanassapaṭilābhan”ti?
verses.english: “But how?”
“Once upon a time, sir, a battle was fought between the gods and the titans.

verses.pali: Tasmiṁ kho pana, bhante, saṅgāme devā jiniṁsu, asurā parājayiṁsu.
verses.english: In that battle the gods won and the titans lost.

verses.pali: Tassa mayhaṁ, bhante, taṁ saṅgāmaṁ abhivijinitvā vijitasaṅgāmassa etadahosi:
verses.english: It occurred to me as victor,

verses.pali: ‘yā ceva dāni dibbā ojā yā ca asurā ojā, ubhayametaṁ devā paribhuñjissantī’ti.
verses.english: ‘Now the gods shall enjoy both the nectar of the gods and the nectar of the titans.’

verses.pali: So kho pana me, bhante, vedapaṭilābho somanassapaṭilābho sadaṇḍāvacaro sasatthāvacaro na nibbidāya na virāgāya na nirodhāya na upasamāya na abhiññāya na sambodhāya na nibbānāya saṁvattati.
verses.english: But sir, that joy and happiness is in the sphere of the rod and the sword. It doesn’t lead to disillusionment, dispassion, cessation, peace, insight, awakening, and extinguishment.

verses.pali: Yo kho pana me ayaṁ, bhante, bhagavato dhammaṁ sutvā vedapaṭilābho somanassapaṭilābho, so adaṇḍāvacaro asatthāvacaro ekantanibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṁvattatī”ti.
verses.english: But the joy and happiness I feel listening to the Buddha’s teaching is not in the sphere of the rod and the sword. It does lead to disillusionment, dispassion, cessation, peace, insight, awakening, and extinguishment.”

verses.pali: “Kiṁ pana tvaṁ, devānaminda, atthavasaṁ sampassamāno evarūpaṁ vedapaṭilābhaṁ somanassapaṭilābhaṁ pavedesī”ti?
verses.english: “But lord of gods, what reason do you see for speaking of such joy and happiness?”

verses.pali: “Cha kho ahaṁ, bhante, atthavase sampassamāno evarūpaṁ vedapaṭilābhaṁ somanassapaṭilābhaṁ pavedemi.
verses.english: “I see six reasons to speak of such joy and happiness, sir.
While staying right here,
remaining in the godly form,
I have gained an extended life:
know this, dear sir.

verses.pali: Imaṁ kho ahaṁ, bhante, paṭhamaṁ atthavasaṁ sampassamāno evarūpaṁ vedapaṭilābhaṁ somanassapaṭilābhaṁ pavedemi.
verses.english: This is the first reason.
When I fall from the heavenly host,
leaving behind the non-human life,
I shall consciously go to a new womb,
wherever my mind delights.

verses.pali: Imaṁ kho ahaṁ, bhante, dutiyaṁ atthavasaṁ sampassamāno evarūpaṁ vedapaṭilābhaṁ somanassapaṭilābhaṁ pavedemi.
verses.english: This is the second reason.
Living happily under the guidance
of the one of unclouded wisdom,
I shall practice systematically,
aware and mindful.

verses.pali: Imaṁ kho ahaṁ, bhante, tatiyaṁ atthavasaṁ sampassamāno evarūpaṁ vedapaṭilābhaṁ somanassapaṭilābhaṁ pavedemi.
verses.english: This is the third reason.
And if awakening should arise
as I practice systematically,
I shall live as one who understands,
and my end shall come right there.

verses.pali: Imaṁ kho ahaṁ, bhante, catutthaṁ atthavasaṁ sampassamāno evarūpaṁ vedapaṭilābhaṁ somanassapaṭilābhaṁ pavedemi.
verses.english: This is the fourth reason.
When I fall from the human realm,
leaving behind the human life,
I shall become a god again,
supreme in the heaven realm.

verses.pali: Imaṁ kho ahaṁ, bhante, pañcamaṁ atthavasaṁ sampassamāno evarūpaṁ vedapaṭilābhaṁ somanassapaṭilābhaṁ pavedemi.
verses.english: This is the fifth reason.
They are the finest of gods,
the glorious Akaniṭṭhas.
So long as my final life goes on,
there my home will be.

verses.pali: Imaṁ kho ahaṁ, bhante, chaṭṭhaṁ atthavasaṁ sampassamāno evarūpaṁ vedapaṭilābhaṁ somanassapaṭilābhaṁ pavedemi.
verses.english: This is the sixth reason.

verses.pali: Ime kho ahaṁ, bhante, cha atthavase sampassamāno evarūpaṁ vedapaṭilābhaṁ somanassapaṭilābhaṁ pavedemi.
verses.english: Seeing these six reasons I speak of such joy and happiness.
My wishes unfulfilled,
doubting and indecisive,
I wandered for such a long time,
in search of the Realized One.
I imagined that ascetics
living in seclusion
must surely be awakened,
so I went to sit near them.
‘How is there success?
How is there failure?’
But they were stumped by such questions
about the path and practice.
And when they found out that I
was Sakka, come from the gods,
they questioned me instead about
the deed that brought me to this state.
I taught them the Dhamma
as I had learned it among men.
They were delighted with that, saying:
‘We’ve seen Vāsava!’
Now since I’ve seen the Buddha,
who helps us overcome doubt,
today, free of fear,
I pay homage to the awakened one.
Destroyer of the dart of craving,
the Buddha is unrivaled.
I bow to the great hero,
the Buddha, Kinsman of the Sun.
In the same way that Divinity ought be revered
by we gods, dear sir,
today we shall revere you—
come, let us revere you ourselves!
You alone are the Awakened!
You are the Teacher supreme!
In the world with its gods,
you have no rival.”

verses.pali: Atha kho sakko devānamindo pañcasikhaṁ gandhabbaputtaṁ āmantesi:
verses.english: Then Sakka addressed the centaur Pañcasikha,

verses.pali: “bahūpakāro kho mesi tvaṁ, tāta pañcasikha, yaṁ tvaṁ bhagavantaṁ paṭhamaṁ pasādesi.
verses.english: “Dear Pañcasikha, you were very helpful to me, since you first charmed the Buddha,

verses.pali: Tayā, tāta, paṭhamaṁ pasāditaṁ pacchā mayaṁ taṁ bhagavantaṁ dassanāya upasaṅkamimhā arahantaṁ sammāsambuddhaṁ.
verses.english: after which I went to see him.

verses.pali: Pettike vā ṭhāne ṭhapayissāmi, gandhabbarājā bhavissasi, bhaddañca te sūriyavacchasaṁ dammi, sā hi te abhipatthitā”ti.
verses.english: I shall appoint you to your father’s position—you shall be king of the centaurs. And I give you Bhaddā Suriyavaccasā, for she loves you very much.”

verses.pali: Atha kho sakko devānamindo pāṇinā pathaviṁ parāmasitvā tikkhattuṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
verses.english: Then Sakka, touching the ground with his hand, expressed this heartfelt sentiment three times:
“Homage to him, the blessed one, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha!
Homage to him, the blessed one, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha!
Homage to him, the blessed one, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha!”

verses.pali: Imasmiñca pana veyyākaraṇasmiṁ bhaññamāne sakkassa devānamindassa virajaṁ vītamalaṁ dhammacakkhuṁ udapādi:
verses.english: And while this discourse was being spoken, the stainless, immaculate vision of the Dhamma arose in Sakka, lord of gods:
“Everything that is liable to arise is liable to cease.”
And also for another 80,000 deities.

verses.pali: iti ye sakkena devānamindena ajjhiṭṭhapañhā puṭṭhā, te bhagavatā byākatā.
verses.english: Such were the questions Sakka was invited to ask, and which were answered by the Buddha.
And that’s why the name of this discussion is “Sakka’s Questions”.
